name: OpsGate
author: opsgate

sections.description:
OpsGate — WordPress Operational Intelligence

OpsGate gives WordPress professionals and agencies a clearer view of what is happening across the sites they manage, what requires attention, and what to do next.

It turns site signals, WordPress inventory, operational checks, security posture, updates, performance, availability, decisions, and history into one operational intelligence workflow.

Instead of working across disconnected tools and raw technical outputs, OpsGate helps you move from:

observe → understand → prioritize → act → verify

Know what needs attention

OpsGate evaluates the current condition of a site and brings the most important operational signals together in context.

Depending on your plan and site connection, OpsGate can surface intelligence across:

  • WordPress core, plugin, and theme inventory
  • Update posture
  • Vulnerability exposure
  • Site availability and reachability
  • SSL/TLS and supported public checks
  • Performance signals
  • Operational changes over time
  • Recorded findings and decisions
  • Reports and exports
  • Alerts and notification workflows
  • Site and portfolio history
  • Multi-site operational intelligence

The objective is not more monitoring noise.

It is a clearer answer to:

What is happening, why does it matter, and where should I focus next?

From one site to an entire portfolio

The WordPress plugin connects the individual site to OpsGate and provides a focused site-level operating surface.

The OpsGate web console at opsgate.ca extends that intelligence across deeper site analysis, reports, alerts, history, account management, and multi-site portfolio operations.

For agencies, OpsGate provides a central operating view across managed WordPress sites so attention can be directed by operational priority rather than by manually checking sites one by one.

Free public intelligence

OpsGate can begin with supported external checks using publicly observable site information.

This mode does not require authenticated access to private WordPress inventory.

Connected intelligence

Connecting a WordPress site allows OpsGate to incorporate supported WordPress-specific information that cannot be obtained reliably through public observation alone.

Connected capabilities vary by plan and may include deeper site triage, operational history, reports, alerts, and portfolio intelligence.

Choose the level of operational intelligence you need

Free — Start with supported public site intelligence using externally observable signals. Free is
designed for an initial view of site condition without requiring authenticated access to private
WordPress inventory.

Starter — Connect one WordPress site for deeper operational intelligence. Starter brings
WordPress-specific inventory and assessment into OpsGate so you can move beyond public observation into
connected site operations.

Pro — Expand from assessment into a broader professional operating workflow. Pro is designed for
professionals managing multiple sites who need deeper reporting, alerts, operational history, and
connected site intelligence.

Agency — Operate across a client portfolio. Agency brings multi-site intelligence, portfolio
prioritization, professional reporting, branding, and agency-level workflows into one OpsGate operating
environment.

The progression is straightforward:

  • Free — observe externally
  • Starter — understand one site deeply
  • Pro — operate professionally across sites
  • Agency — command a client portfolio

Available capabilities depend on the active OpsGate plan.

Built for professional operations

OpsGate is designed for people responsible for keeping WordPress sites reliable, secure, current, and accountable.

That includes:

  • independent WordPress professionals
  • managed-service providers
  • agencies
  • technical operations teams
  • organizations responsible for multiple WordPress properties

OpsGate is not intended to replace professional judgment.

It is designed to make that judgment faster, better informed, and easier to support with operational history.

External Service

OpsGate is a hosted service operated by Cyber Eclipse in Quebec, Canada.

The WordPress plugin communicates with the OpsGate service through:

https://api.opsgate.ca

This endpoint provides the secure application interface used to connect the WordPress site with OpsGate.

Depending on the operation and connection state, information transmitted to OpsGate may include:

  • the site URL;
  • supported WordPress environment information;
  • installed plugin and theme information;
  • supported version and update information;
  • operational information required for enabled OpsGate assessments.

Public assessments use supported publicly observable site information and do not require authenticated access to private WordPress inventory.

Connected assessments require an authorized OpsGate site connection.

Information is transmitted when an OpsGate operation requires it, such as connecting a site, running an assessment, or refreshing connected site information.

The WordPress.org version of OpsGate receives plugin updates through WordPress.org.

Terms of Service: https://opsgate.ca/terms

Privacy Policy: https://opsgate.ca/privacy
sections.installation:
Install OpsGate

  1. In WordPress Admin, open Plugins → Add New Plugin.
  2. Search for OpsGate.
  3. Select Install Now.
  4. Activate the plugin.
  5. Open OpsGate from the WordPress Admin menu.

Start with a public assessment

You can begin with supported public site intelligence without connecting private WordPress inventory.

Enter or select the site and follow the OpsGate workflow.

Connect the WordPress site

For deeper connected intelligence:

  1. Sign in to your OpsGate account at opsgate.ca.
  2. Add or select the WordPress site.
  3. Start the site connection.
  4. Complete the secure pairing process in WordPress.
  5. Return to OpsGate to continue with the connected site.

Available capabilities depend on the active OpsGate plan.
sections.faq:
Who is OpsGate for?

OpsGate is designed for WordPress professionals, agencies, and teams responsible for operating one or more WordPress sites.

Do I need to connect my WordPress site to start?

No.

OpsGate can perform supported external checks using publicly observable site information.

Connecting the site unlocks deeper WordPress-specific intelligence according to your plan.

What changes when I connect a site?

A connected site can provide OpsGate with supported WordPress environment and inventory information that is unavailable through public observation alone.

This allows OpsGate to deliver deeper assessment, history, reporting, alerting, and operational workflows.

Can OpsGate manage multiple WordPress sites?

Yes. Multi-site and portfolio capabilities are available according to the active OpsGate plan.

Where do I use OpsGate?

The WordPress plugin provides the local site connection and site-level operating experience.

The broader OpsGate workspace is available at opsgate.ca.

Does OpsGate automatically modify my WordPress site?

OpsGate does not perform an operational change merely because it identifies a condition.

Where an action or automation capability is available, the product makes the intended action explicit and operates within the permissions and controls provided by the applicable service.
sections.changelog:
0.10.8

  • Introduced the current OpsGate WordPress companion experience.
  • Improved site connection and pairing workflows.
  • Added clearer site condition, account, and connection context.
  • Improved navigation between WordPress and the OpsGate web console.
  • Improved connected-site recovery and support diagnostics.
  • General reliability and compatibility improvements.

Earlier releases

Earlier development releases established the initial OpsGate connection, assessment, reporting, alerting, and site-management foundations.

Site Scan - Detailed assessment across WordPress inventory, operational checks, findings, ownership, and verification.
Operations Dashboard - Site behavior, posture, changes, and operational intelligence across time.
Portfolio Intelligence - Prioritize attention across multiple managed WordPress sites.
Reports - Turn operational activity and site condition into professional client-ready reporting.
Alerts - Configure how important operational changes are surfaced.
Activity and history - Review the sequence of runs, findings, decisions, reports, alerts, and recorded operational events.
